newsitem.title: USA: Palestinian shoots tourists on Empire State Building.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian shoots tourists on Empire State Building.

text.p: A man identified as a 69-year old Palestinian fired into a crowd of tourists on the observation deck of the famous Empire State Building on Sunday, killing one person and wounding six others before shooting himself.

Police said the gunman, Ali Abu Kamal, died without regaining consciousness in a New York hospital, several hours after he wielded a semi-automatic handgun at tourists on the outdoor observation deck on the 86th floor of the building.

New York Mayor Rudolph Giuliani told a news conference the gunman was carrying documents from the Palestinian Authoritiy that showed he lived in Ramallah on the West Bank and was born in Jaffa. He came to New York on Christmas Eve.
Kamal had bought the pistol used in the shooting in Florida at the end of January, the mayor said. Police said a receipt for the gun was found on his body.
"He began opening fire and shot at least eight times, hitting seven people and obviously himself," Giuliani said.
The incident, he said, "created a great deal of pandemonium." "It was very crowded, typical for a Sunday afternoon."

The dead tourist was a 27-year old musician from Denmark, who was visiting the Empire State Building, one of the world's most famous tourist attractions. He was with a musician friend from Connecticut, who was injured, Giuliani reported.

Others wounded, all in serious or critical condition, included a 52-year-old Argentine man, a 30-year-old Swiss man, a 35-year old Bronx, N.Y. man and a couple from Verdun, France. Their 16-year old daughter escaped injury, Giuliani said.
He said a joint terrorism task force of the Federal Bureau of Investigation and city police would investigate the shootings.

It was not known whether the incident was politically motivated. "There are various reports that different things were said by this man. None have been verified," the mayor said, without giving further details.
"There is no indication at this point that there is any other incident connected to the gunman," the mayor said.

On Feb. 26, 1993, a massive bomb exploded in the garage of the World Trade Centre, killing six people and injuring more than 1,000. Four Moslem militants were convicted and sentenced to life in prison for the bombing.

The shooting occurred at about 5 p.m. EST (2200 GMT) and sent hundreds of tourists on the 86th floor of the skyscraper scattering for safety. Witnesses said they dived to the floor as bursts of fire rang out.

A spokeswoman for Bellevue Hospital said a five-month old boy and his 18-month old sister were treated for minor injuries and later released from the hospital. Giuliani, who earlier had given different ages for the children, said they were knocked to the ground in the confusion.

A building security camera tape was turned over to police, said Howard Rubenstein, a spokesman for building, which does not have metal detectors. It shows the gunman on the way up to the observation deck.
"He was wearing a long coat. The gun was not visible and presumably it was hidden under his coat," Rubenstein said.

A one-block area surrounding the Empire State Building at Fifth Avenue and 34th Street in Manhattan was blocked off for hours as dozens of ambulances, police and fire trucks converged on the area. It was opened to traffic again later in the evening.

The Empire State Building, which opened in 1931, is one of New York City's top tourist attractions, and at 1,250 feet (380 metres) high with 102 floors, it ranked for decades as the world's tallest building. In 1972, the Art Deco landmark was overtaken by the twin towers of the World Trade Centre.

The skyscraper has been featured in hundreds of movies, including the 1933 climactic scene of the film classic, "King Kong", in which the giant ape clung to its side as he battled a squadron of attacking planes. The observation deck was also a romantic site for such films as "Sleepless in Seattle" and "An Affair To Remember".
